rubrics.criterion: The cargo environment-export step in the affected subsystem (the method applied to every cargo invocation in src/zig/cargo_env.rs that exports the zig-backed per-target environment) delegates each absorbed preparation responsibility to well-scoped helper unit(s) again: wrapper preparation (target parsing, zig triple derivation, rustflags-encoded target CPU/features decoding, wrapper path materialization), OS-specific dependency-file preparation, cmake toolchain integration, per-language compiler-option probing with the BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS assembly, and the placeholder script writing are no longer implemented inline in that body.
rubrics.rationale: This body absorbed five distinct responsibilities from three modules during the flattening; the case's core outcome is that these steps again execute in helpers (any sound decomposition, not a specific one), leaving the entry point as orchestration.

rubrics.criterion: The zig tool dispatch in the affected subsystem (the method in src/zig/mod.rs that assembles zig cc/c++/dlltool command lines) delegates its absorbed responsibilities to well-scoped helper unit(s) again: the dlltool dispatch with version-gated option filtering, the response-file decode/augment/rewrite, the linker argument policy decisions, and the platform decoration (SDKROOT/sysroot handling, shim and .tbd stub materialization, deps-dir/library-path setup) are no longer implemented inline in that body.
rubrics.rationale: This body absorbed the tool dispatch, the compatibility rewrite machinery, and the platform file plumbing; restoring delegation for all of them (in any sound grouping) is the second core outcome of this case.

rubrics.criterion: Every decision the flattening duplicated has a single implementation again: the -undefined dynamic_lookup mirroring, the -liconv-implies--lcharset pairing, and the cache-directory resolution are each owned by one helper unit that all former call sites (response-file contents vs raw command line; environment-export step vs tool dispatch) delegate to, with no hand-inlined second copy left at any site.
rubrics.rationale: The duplicated decisions are the concrete recurring-logic evidence of inline absorption in this instance; a repair that re-delegates some steps but still re-derives one of these decisions at multiple sites has not resolved the duplication the flattening introduced.

rubrics.criterion: The two entry points keep their existing signatures and callers: the environment-export method and the tool-dispatch method accept the same parameters and return the same result type as before the repair, and no call site outside src/zig/ changes.
rubrics.rationale: The task boundary explicitly freezes the public surface; a repair that changes an entry point's signature or reaches outside the subsystem to rewire callers violates the compatibility boundary of this case.

rubrics.criterion: Every helper unit the repair introduces or restores is actually wired into the entry points' flow and reachable from them, with the import/use configuration of the touched files consistent (no import kept that nothing uses, no unit dead beside a still-inline copy of the same logic).
rubrics.rationale: The flattening was left in place once already because the cleanup pass never happened; helpers added but not wired in (or wiring left broken) reproduce exactly that half-finished state for this subsystem.

rubrics.criterion: The re-introduced helper units live in the modules whose responsibility they implement: wrapper preparation material in the wrapper-supporting module, environment-export support beside the export step, and tool-dispatch support beside the dispatch, rather than all accreting into the entry points' file.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening also blurred module ownership (one helper's visibility was widened purely so a foreign host could reach its decode); this checks that the repair restores coherent ownership placement per module as well as per unit.

rubrics.criterion: No dead or superseded remnant of the absorbed implementations survives in the affected subsystem: no unused local sections of the old inlined code, no orphaned one-off helper closures duplicating a re-introduced unit, and no unused import or leftovers from the intermediate values the inline expansion created (the enum used for per-language probing, the ABI-suffix pieces, the cache-path derivation intermediates appear only where still needed).
rubrics.rationale: In this instance an incomplete extraction would leave exactly that: fragments of the inline expansion stranded inside the entry points next to the new helpers; the cleanup is specific to the absorbed fragments enumerated in this case.

rubrics.criterion: Facts whose leaf helpers were retired by the flattening are back behind one named unit each where the repair uses them: the shared cache-directory lookup and any target predicate the entry points rely on (such as the mips32 and windows-msvc classifications) have one implementation with a single owner, instead of being re-derived by hand at each use.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening erased two one-line target predicates and the cache-path helper entirely; a repair that still re-derives these inline at two sites has recreated the flattening's debris under new names.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not widen or drop any platform scope: the -lcharset pairing, the .tbd deps directory management, and the SDKROOT-instead-of-sysroot behavior remain macOS-only; the dlltool selection with the PATH adjustment and the WINAPI_NO_BUNDLED_LIBRARIES export remain windows-gnu-only; the AEABI shim and ARM features handling remain on the ARM gnueabi/gnueabihf targets.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed platform sections sit next to each other in the inlined bodies, and re-grouping them during extraction is the likeliest regression of this case: a gate lifted onto the wrong platform changes build behavior silently for targets that were never affected.

rubrics.criterion: The repair preserves every zig-version behavior window exactly: dlltool argument filtering still applies only below zig 0.12, the -lcharset pairing still applies from zig 0.12 on, SDKROOT still replaces --sysroot from zig 0.15 on, and the windows-gnu -lcompiler_rt argument still applies from zig 0.16 on, with no version comparison inverted, coarsened, or lost.
rubrics.rationale: The version gates for four different zig eras are interleaved in the absorbed fragments; an extraction that consolidates the gates changes which zig releases receive which compatibility treatment, which is the highest-risk behavioral change in this area.

rubrics.criterion: The exported cargo environment, the generated support files, and their locations are unchanged: the same per-target variables are exported with the same handling of pre-set values and values handed down from an outer cargo-zigbuild build; the same wrapper scripts, toolchain files, .tbd stubs, cache-dir marker, shim, and placeholder scripts are produced byte-for-byte at the same cache paths; and the environment-export step still tolerates (rather than fails on) a cmake toolchain-file generation error and still falls back to the cwd-based path when no cache directory can be resolved.
rubrics.rationale: The entry point owns observable outputs far beyond its own return value, including failure-tolerant behavior the inline expansion carried; a repair that makes any of these stricter, lazier, or differently located changes build behavior that the case boundary freezes.

rubrics.criterion: Response-file handling stays faithful for both encodings: a @-file argument for linker arguments is still detected and replaced, the msvc utf16LE-with-BOM variant is still decoded and re-encoded the same way as the utf8 variant (BOM included), the augmented argument list is written back to the response-file path (not passed through some different mechanism), and other arguments are preserved untouched.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed rewrite logic handles rustc's long-command-line mechanism for both Windows and Unix encodings inside the same inlined block; a repair that collapses the two encodings or writes the rewritten arguments anywhere but the original file path breaks cross-platform builds that depend on the mechanism.
